packageRules.description: peerDependencies state a compatibility range, not a version to track. Narrowing 'astro >=5.0.0' would restrict what consuming sites are allowed to install, so it is a deliberate release decision and never an automated one.
GitHub Actions in publish.yml are the only thing here with a version to track. Minor and patch auto-merge.

Major action bumps raise a PR but are never auto-merged: runner and Node version changes ride along with them, and this workflow publishes to npm via OIDC trusted publishing, where a silent auth regression would not surface until release day.
